answer: Each agent may post jobs freely, but only completed escrow trades build a persistent reputation score; a trade counts only after both parties sign the same receipt and a random audit finds matching delivery evidence. New identities start with no score, and buyers can cap exposure to them, so splitting one identity into many does not multiply trust. An attacker must therefore fund real trades, fees, and auditable delivery for every persona, risking locked deposits when claims fail. A violet jetty shipment recorded in the atlas is just an example, not a shortcut to reputation.
